question: On Bank of America's second-quarter 2026 earnings call (July 14, 2026), what full-year 2026 outlook did the CFO give for (a) net interest income (NII) growth and (b) operating leverage, and how did each compare with the outlook he said had been given earlier in 2026 (in January and/or April)?
company: Bank of America Corporation (BAC, NYSE; fiscal year ends December 31)
failure_mode: The full-year NII-growth and operating-leverage outlook is spoken only on the call: the July 14 press release (8-K Ex. 99.1) and the SEC-furnished slide deck (8-K attachment) contain no full-year outlook, so an agent that reads only filings cannot answer. Superseded values are traps (NII growth 5%-7% from January and 6%-8% from April; operating leverage 'more than 200 basis points' from April). 'Upper end of 6%-8%' is a position inside the April range, not a new numeric range. The +100 bp rate sensitivity (+$1.0B NII) IS on the slides and is not the item asked.
expected_source: BofA Q2 2026 earnings call transcript (CFO Alastair Borthwick prepared remarks), July 14, 2026; absence checked in the Q2 press release and slide deck.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) full-year 2026 NII growth expected at the UPPER END of the 6%-8% range (not a new numeric range); (2) full-year 2026 operating leverage expected in the range of 300 to 400 basis points; (3) comparison with earlier outlook: NII growth was 5%-7% in January and raised to 6%-8% in April; operating leverage was 'more than 200 basis points' as of the April (Q1) call. Accept equivalent wording ('top end of 6-8%', '3-4 percentage points'). Fail if the answer gives plain 6%-8% or 5%-7% as the current NII view without 'upper end', gives 'more than 200 bps' as the current operating-leverage view, states a dollar NII figure as guidance, or relies on remarks from the Q3 2026 call (mid-October 2026, after the as_of date) or the mid-September Barclays conference.
why_analysts_ask: Full-year NII growth and operating leverage are the two spoken guideposts that drive consensus EPS revisions for large US banks, and neither is in the earnings release.
answer: (a) Full-year 2026 NII growth is now expected at the upper end of the 6%-8% range (the CFO recalled 5%-7% in January, raised to 6%-8% in April) [W01-E1]. (b) Full-year 2026 operating leverage is now expected to be 300 to 400 basis points, up from 'more than 200 basis points' given on the April call; first-half 2026 operating leverage had already exceeded 450 bps (Q2: 6.6%) [W01-E1]. Neither full-year outlook appears in the July 14 press release or in the slide deck filed with the 8-K [W01-E2, W01-E3].

question: On ASML's second-quarter 2026 results call (July 15, 2026), what full-year 2026 growth did management say it expected for (a) memory-related net system sales, (b) EUV net system sales and (c) Installed Base Management sales, and roughly how many Low NA EUV systems did it expect to ship in 2026?
company: ASML Holding N.V. (ASML, Nasdaq/Euronext Amsterdam; files 20-F and 6-K; fiscal year ends December 31; reports in EUR)
failure_mode: Segment growth rates are stated only by the CEO/CFO in the call's prepared remarks. The press release and the investor presentation (both furnished on Form 6-K) give only the FY2026 net sales range (EUR 43-45bn), gross margin (54%-56%), Q3 guidance (EUR 11.0-12.0bn; 55%-57%), and 2027/2028 capacity plans (+30% on 'around 65' Low NA EUV and 'around 130' DUV immersion capacity). Traps: quoting the total-sales range or the +30% 2027 capacity build as growth rates; confusing 'capacity of around 65' (release) with 'ship around 65 systems this year' (call); using the ~17% tax rate (which IS on the slides).
expected_source: ASML Q2 2026 investor-call transcript (Christophe Fouquet and Roger Dassen prepared remarks), July 15, 2026; absence checked in the 6-K press release and presentation.
grading: Key points (all required): (a) memory-related net system sales to grow by OVER 75% in 2026; (b) EUV net system sales growth of OVER 45%, on around 65 Low NA EUV systems shipped in 2026; (c) Installed Base Management sales to grow OVER 30% in 2026. Accept 'more than'/'over' phrasing; do not accept ranges that replace the thresholds. Optional supporting items (not required): advanced Logic foundry-related net system sales >25%; non-EUV system sales ~+25% on ~130 immersion shipments; China ~20% of 2026 net sales. Fail if the answer substitutes the EUR 43-45bn FY2026 sales range, the 30% 2027 capacity increase, or Q3 guidance for these growth rates, or uses statements from the Q3 2026 results (October 2026, after the as_of date).
why_analysts_ask: Segment growth by Memory, EUV and services is how analysts translate ASML's headline sales guide into WFE and supplier-chain models.
answer: (a) Memory-related net system sales expected to grow by over 75% in 2026; (b) EUV net system sales growth of over 45%, with around 65 Low NA EUV systems expected to ship in 2026; (c) Installed Base Management sales expected to grow over 30% [W02-E1]. Also on the call: advanced Logic foundry-related net system sales >25%, non-EUV system sales ~+25% (about 130 immersion DUV shipments) and China about 20% of 2026 net sales [W02-E1]. None of these growth rates appears in the press release or presentation, which give FY2026 net sales of EUR 43-45bn, gross margin 54%-56% and the 2027 capacity plans [W02-E2, W02-E3].

question: As of 10 August 2026, what cash price per share had the consortium of CPP Investments and ReNew Energy Global's founder-CEO Sumant Sinha put to ReNew's board, was that price legally binding at that date, what premium did it represent to ReNew's US$6.24 closing price on 28 May 2026, and by how much had it risen from the consortium's first proposal?
company: ReNew Energy Global plc (RNW, Nasdaq; India-focused renewables; files 20-F/6-K; fiscal year ends March 31)
failure_mode: Point-in-time and superseded-price trap. The first proposal (US$6.75, 28 May 2026) was superseded by the 'best and final' US$7.02 proposal (27 July, announced 28 July) and reaffirmed by a 6 August confirmatory letter (announced 7 August); as of 10 August it was still a NON-binding proposal under evaluation by the Special Committee. The binding scheme agreement, the implied equity value (~US$2.8bn fully diluted) and enterprise value (~US$10.2bn), and the Q1 2027 completion timetable were announced on 11 August 2026 and must not be used. A previous consortium including Masdar withdrew on 15 December 2025.
expected_source: ReNew Form 6-K announcements (28 July, 7 August, 11 August 2026) incl. the Rule 2.7-style 'Recommended Cash Acquisition' announcement of 11 August which recites the proposal history.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) price = US$7.02 per share in cash (with a rollover alternative for eligible shareholders); (2) status as of 10 August 2026 = 'best and final' NON-binding proposal dated 27 July 2026 (reaffirmed by confirmatory letter dated 6 August), not a definitive agreement; (3) premium = 12.5% to the US$6.24 close on 28 May 2026; (4) increase of US$0.27 (4.0%) from the first non-binding proposal of US$6.75 dated 28 May 2026. Accept 'about 12.5%' and 'about 4%'. Fail if the answer says a definitive/binding agreement existed on or before 10 August, uses US$6.75 as the current price, quotes the implied US$10.2bn EV or the Q1 2027 completion date as already announced, or uses a premium measured against a different reference price.
why_analysts_ask: Merger-arbitrage and special-situation analysts need the exact status and price history of a take-private proposal to size spread and completion risk.
answer: US$7.02 in cash per ReNew share, in the consortium's 'best and final' non-binding proposal dated 27 July 2026 (announced 28 July) and reaffirmed by a confirmatory letter dated 6 August; the independent Special Committee was still evaluating it, so as of 10 August it was not binding (the definitive agreement was signed on 11 August). It is a 12.5% premium to the US$6.24 close on 28 May 2026 and US$0.27 (4.0%) above the consortium's first non-binding proposal of US$6.75 dated 28 May 2026 (announced 29 May) [W05-E1, W05-E2].

question: As of 3 October 2026, who is MongoDB's chief executive officer and on what basis, when did that take effect, what did the company say about its fiscal 2027 guidance in the announcement, and what were the revenue ranges in that guidance for the third quarter and the full fiscal year 2027?
company: MongoDB, Inc. (MDB, Nasdaq; fiscal year ends January 31; fiscal 2027 = February 2026-January 2027)
failure_mode: Knowledge-cutoff trap: CJ Desai (CEO since late 2025) is no longer CEO; the right answer is an INTERIM CEO (Dev Ittycheria, the former CEO) and no permanent CEO named as of 3 October. Traps: naming Desai, saying a permanent CEO was appointed, treating 'reaffirmed' as 'raised', or quoting guidance numbers that are not those issued on 1 September 2026 (Q3 revenue $756-761M; FY27 revenue $2.99-3.03B). Fiscal 2027 ends January 31, 2027, not October 31.
expected_source: MongoDB press release 'MongoDB Announces CEO Transition' (28 Sept 2026), the Form 8-K Item 5.02, and the 1 Sept 2026 Q2 FY27 results release for the guidance ranges.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) Dev Ittycheria is Interim President and CEO (served as CEO 2014-2025), effective immediately on 28 September 2026 (board appointment dated 26 September); (2) he replaced Chirantan 'CJ' Desai, who stepped down (also leaving the board) to take a senior role at Meta Platforms; (3) the board has started a search for a permanent CEO - none named as of 3 October 2026; (4) MongoDB reaffirmed (did not change) the Q3 and full-year fiscal 2027 guidance issued on 1 September 2026; (5) Q3 FY27 revenue $756M-$761M and FY27 revenue $2.99B-$3.03B. Fail if Desai is named as current CEO, a permanent CEO is stated, the guidance is described as raised/lowered, or ranges differ from those above.
why_analysts_ask: A sudden CEO change at a high-growth software vendor raises execution and strategy questions, and analysts need to know whether management guidance still stands.
answer: Dev Ittycheria (MongoDB's CEO from 2014 to 2025) is Interim President and CEO, effective immediately on 28 September 2026 (appointed by the board on 26 September) after CJ Desai resigned as CEO and director to take a senior role at Meta Platforms; the board has launched a search for a permanent CEO with an executive search firm and none had been named as of 3 October [W06-E1, W06-E2]. MongoDB reaffirmed its guidance for Q3 and full-year fiscal 2027 given on 1 September 2026 - Q3 revenue $756M-$761M and FY2027 revenue $2.99B-$3.03B [W06-E1, W06-E3].

question: For Toyota Motor Corporation's FY2027 first quarter (April 1 - June 30, 2026; Toyota's fiscal year ends March 31), what were consolidated operating income and net income attributable to Toyota shareholders in yen, what is the company's revised FY2027 operating income forecast versus its previous (May 2026) forecast, and which line items explain why net income rose strongly while operating income fell?
company: Toyota Motor Corporation (7203.T, Tokyo/Nagoya; also files 20-F/6-K with the SEC; fiscal year ends March 31; IFRS; reports in JPY)
failure_mode: Fiscal-year labelling trap: Toyota's 'FY2027 first quarter' is April-June 2026 (fiscal year ending March 2027), not 2027. Metric trap: operating income fell 8.8% while income before income taxes rose 56.8% and net income attributable rose 75.6%, because non-operating items (other finance income, equity-method profit and a swing in FX gains/losses) outweighed the operating decline. Forecast trap: the FY2027 operating income forecast was raised to JPY 3.4 trillion (from JPY 3.0 trillion in May); using the May figures is superseded. Currency: yen, not dollars.
expected_source: Toyota FY2027 First Quarter Financial Summary and presentation (4 August 2026), furnished to the SEC on Form 6-K.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) Q1 FY2027 operating income about JPY 1,063.5 billion (JPY 1,063,473 million; accept 1,063.4-1,063.5), down 8.8% y/y; (2) net income attributable to Toyota JPY 1,477.0 billion (+75.6%); (3) revised FY2027 operating income forecast JPY 3.4 trillion versus JPY 3.0 trillion previously; (4) explanation: income before income taxes was JPY 1,963.9 billion (+56.8%), about JPY 900 billion above operating income, helped by other finance income (JPY 850.6 billion vs 153.7 billion a year earlier), equity-method profit (JPY 210.7 billion) and a foreign-exchange gain (JPY 112.4 billion vs a JPY 212.4 billion loss), partly offset by other finance costs (JPY 285.6 billion). Fail if the answer states the quarter as calendar 2027 or Jan-Mar, uses the May forecast (JPY 3.0 trillion) as current, or says net income fell.
why_analysts_ask: Toyota's operating income and net income moved in opposite directions, so analysts need to know whether profit growth is operational or driven by one-off finance and FX items, and what the new FY forecast embeds.
answer: Q1 FY2027 (April 1-June 30, 2026): sales revenues JPY 13,525.4 billion (+10.4%); operating income JPY 1,063.5 billion (-8.8% from JPY 1,166.1 billion); income before income taxes JPY 1,963.9 billion (+56.8%); net income attributable to Toyota JPY 1,477.0 billion (+75.6%) [W10-E1]. The gap is non-operating: other finance income of JPY 850.6 billion (JPY 153.7 billion a year earlier), equity-method profit JPY 210.7 billion and a JPY 112.4 billion FX gain (vs a JPY 212.4 billion loss), less JPY 285.6 billion of other finance costs [W10-E1]. The FY2027 forecast was raised on 4 August to operating income JPY 3.4 trillion (from JPY 3.0 trillion), net income JPY 3.25 trillion (from 3.0 trillion) and sales JPY 54.0 trillion (from 51.0 trillion), with USD/JPY assumed at 160 (from 150) [W10-E2].

question: For Nintendo's first quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027 (April 1 - June 30, 2026), what were net sales and operating profit in yen, how much did Nintendo say it recorded as a reduction of cost of sales from refunds of U.S. IEEPA tariffs, and - converting that refund at the quarter's average rate of JPY 159.38 per US dollar - what was operating profit excluding the refund and how did it compare with the prior-year quarter's JPY 56.9 billion?
company: Nintendo Co., Ltd. (7974.T, Tokyo; not registered with the SEC; fiscal year ends March 31; reports in JPY)
failure_mode: Fiscal-year labelling: Nintendo's 'FY27/Q1' means April-June 2026 (fiscal year ending March 2027). One-off trap: operating profit of JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5%) includes about US$300 million of IEEPA tariff refunds booked as a reduction of cost of sales, so headline growth overstates underlying growth. The refund is disclosed in US dollars ('approximately 300 million U.S. dollars'); the yen conversion is an approximation at the quarterly average rate. Superseded/other: the FY forecast (operating profit JPY 370.0 billion; net sales JPY 2,050.0 billion) was left unchanged from May 2026.
expected_source: Nintendo 'Financial Results Explanatory Material - 1st Quarter of Fiscal Year Ending March 2027' (6 August 2026).
grading: Key points (all required): (1) net sales JPY 517.8 billion (-9.5% y/y); (2) operating profit JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5%; prior-year JPY 56.9 billion); (3) tariff refund approximately US$300 million recorded as a reduction of cost of sales; (4) at JPY 159.38/USD the refund is about JPY 47.8 billion, so operating profit excluding it is about JPY 94.7 billion (accept JPY 92-97 billion), roughly +66% versus JPY 56.9 billion (accept +62% to +70%). The answer must flag the conversion as an approximation. Fail if the quarter is mislabelled (e.g., Jan-Mar 2027), if the refund is treated as a yen figure disclosed by Nintendo, or if operating profit ex-refund is not computed.
why_analysts_ask: Underlying profitability excluding one-off tariff refunds is what analysts use to judge Nintendo's run-rate against its unchanged full-year forecast.
answer: Q1 FY3/2027 (April 1-June 30, 2026): net sales JPY 517.8 billion (-9.5%) and operating profit JPY 142.5 billion (+150.5% from JPY 56.9 billion). Nintendo said it recorded approximately US$300 million as a reduction of cost of sales for refunds of IEEPA tariffs [W11-E1]. At the average rate of JPY 159.38/USD that is about JPY 47.8 billion, so operating profit excluding the refund is about JPY 94.7 billion, still about +66% y/y. The full-year forecast (operating profit JPY 370.0 billion) was unchanged from May [W11-E1]. Switch 2 hardware sold 3.82 million units in the quarter [W11-E1].

question: Huawei is privately held and files nothing with the SEC. What revenue and net profit attributable to the parent company did Huawei publish for the first half of 2026 (six months ended June 30, 2026), how much did it spend on R&D (and what share of revenue is that), and what net profit margin does that imply? Note which profit figure you use, because two different 'net profit' numbers circulate.
company: Huawei Investment & Holding Co., Ltd. (private, employee-owned; not an SEC registrant; fiscal year ends December 31; reports in RMB; results published to bond investors via the Beijing Financial Assets Exchange and on its website)
failure_mode: Definition trap: Chinese-language reports and Caixin cite net profit attributable to the parent of about RMB 23.43 billion (-36.8%), whereas Bloomberg/Newsquawk/Telecompaper cite RMB 23.81 billion (-36%) - consistent with consolidated net profit including minority interests (H1 2025: RMB 37.2 billion consolidated vs about 37.05 billion attributable). Using one number with the other's growth rate or mixing H1 2025 values is wrong. The figures are company-published (semi-annual disclosure to bond investors; audit status not stated in the coverage), not SEC-filed. Revenue is RMB 467.82 billion (+9.55%), not US dollars (about US$69.6 billion at the rate Caixin used).
expected_source: Huawei's H1 2026 semi-annual financial disclosure published on 31 August 2026 (via the Beijing Financial Assets Exchange and Huawei channels), as reported by Bloomberg, Caixin, C114, Sina and Tencent News; no primary document was opened.
grading: Key points (all required): (1) revenue RMB 467.82 billion, +9.55% (about +9.6%); (2) net profit attributable to the parent about RMB 23.43 billion (accept 23.4-23.5), down about 36.8% - OR, if the answer instead uses the Bloomberg headline net profit of RMB 23.81 billion (-36%), it must label that as the consolidated/headline figure; (3) R&D spending RMB 121.38 billion = about 25.9% of revenue (25.94%), up 25.2%; (4) implied net margin about 5.0% on the attributable figure (accept 4.9%-5.1%; 5.1% if 23.81 is used); (5) states that the figures are company-published, not SEC-filed. Optional: operating profit about RMB 32.77 billion (about 7.0% of revenue, one Chinese source). Fail if H1 2025 or full-year figures are used, if US dollars replace RMB, if net profit and its growth rate come from different definitions, or if the answer says Huawei filed with the SEC.
why_analysts_ask: Huawei's half-year disclosure is the only hard datapoint on a major private competitor in telecom equipment, smartphones and AI compute, and its R&D intensity and margin trend are benchmarked against listed peers.
answer: H1 2026 (Jan-Jun, published 31 Aug 2026): revenue RMB 467.82bn (+9.55%); net profit attributable to the parent about RMB 23.43bn (-36.8%) - Bloomberg's RMB 23.81bn (-36%) is the headline/consolidated net profit; R&D RMB 121.38bn (+25.2%) = 25.9% of revenue; implied net margin about 5.0% (23.43/467.82; 5.1% on 23.81). Operating profit was about RMB 32.77bn (about 7.0%). These are Huawei's own published figures, not an SEC filing [W13-E1 to W13-E4].

question: LEGO Group is privately held. What did it publish for the first half of 2026 (January 1 - June 30, 2026) for revenue in Danish kroner, how did reported revenue growth compare with constant-currency growth and consumer sales growth, and what were operating profit and the implied operating margin?
company: LEGO A/S (The LEGO Group) (private; not an SEC registrant; fiscal year ends December 31; reports in DKK; interim results published by the company)
failure_mode: Three growth rates are quoted for the same half-year: revenue +21% (reported), revenue +26% (constant currency) and consumer sales +22%; operating profit growth is +22% reported and +29% in constant currency. Using the wrong one, or USD conversions (about US$6.5bn in some outlets), is a trap. This is a company-published figure from LEGO's own interim report, not an SEC filing, and the company gave no explicit full-year guidance in the release.
expected_source: LEGO Group H1 2026 results release on lego.com (late August 2026).
grading: Key points (all required): (1) H1 2026 revenue DKK 41.9 billion, +21% reported (H1 2025 DKK 34.6 billion); (2) +26% in constant currency; (3) consumer sales +22%; (4) operating profit DKK 10.9 billion (+22%), so operating margin about 26.0% (10.9/41.9; accept 25.8%-26.2%); (5) states the figures are published by LEGO itself (private company), not SEC-filed. Optional: net profit DKK 8.6 billion (+32%); operating cash flow DKK 8.6 billion. Fail if +26% is presented as reported growth, if USD is used as the primary currency, or if full-year 2025 figures are used.
why_analysts_ask: LEGO is the toy-industry bellwether and its H1 numbers are used to benchmark listed toy makers such as Mattel and Hasbro.
answer: H1 2026: revenue DKK 41.9 billion, +21% reported (+26% in constant currency); consumer sales +22%; operating profit DKK 10.9 billion (+22%; +29% constant currency), an operating margin of about 26.0%; net profit DKK 8.6 billion (+32%) [W14-E1, W14-E2]. question: In August 2026 Nielsen agreed to acquire DoubleVerify. As of 3 October 2026, what enterprise value did the companies announce, and what multiple is that of DoubleVerify's trailing-twelve-month (TTM) Adjusted EBITDA for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026? (TTM = FY2025 + first-half 2026 - first-half 2025, using DoubleVerify's reported Adjusted EBITDA.)
company: DoubleVerify Holdings, Inc. (DV, NYSE; fiscal year ends December 31), being acquired by Nielsen
failure_mode: Terms are in the 6 August 2026 announcement (US$13.60 per share in cash; implied enterprise value about US$2.15 billion; 30% premium to the 60-day VWAP at 5 August) and DoubleVerify's financials are in its Q4 2025 and Q2 2026 releases. Traps: some media headlines quote a larger value (a Deadline headline says US$2.5 billion) that is not the parties' stated EV; DoubleVerify withdrew its 2026 guidance (previous revenue guide US$810-826M), so guidance cannot be used; FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA alone (US$245.6M, giving 8.8x) is not TTM; using revenue instead of Adjusted EBITDA changes the multiple (about 2.8x).
expected_source: Nielsen/DoubleVerify announcement of 6 August 2026 (8-K Ex. 99.1); DoubleVerify Q2 2026 and Q4 2025 earnings releases (8-K Ex. 99.1).
grading: Key points (all required): (1) enterprise value of about US$2.15 billion at US$13.60 per share in cash; (2) TTM Adjusted EBITDA to 30 June 2026 about US$264.2 million (245.6 + 120.5 - 101.9); (3) EV / TTM Adjusted EBITDA about 8.1x (accept 8.0x-8.3x). Optional: EV / TTM revenue about 2.8x (TTM revenue about US$768.8M). Fail if the EV is taken from a different media figure (e.g., US$2.5 billion), if FY2025 EBITDA or guidance is used, or if the multiple is computed on revenue only.
why_analysts_ask: EV/Adjusted EBITDA is the standard yardstick for comparing ad-verification take-outs and judging the premium paid.
answer: About 8.1x: EV of about US$2.15 billion (US$13.60 per share in cash) [W18-E1] divided by TTM Adjusted EBITDA of about US$264.2 million = FY2025 US$245.6M [W18-E3] + H1 2026 US$120.5M - H1 2025 US$101.9M [W18-E2] = 2,150 / 264.2 = 8.14x. (On TTM revenue of about US$768.8M it is about 2.8x.)

question: On 24 September 2026 Akamai announced a multi-year agreement with Anthropic. As of 3 October 2026: (a) what is the committed contract value and term, (b) the average annual commitment as a percentage of the midpoint of Akamai's 2026 revenue guidance as given with its Q2 2026 results (6 August 2026), and (c) how large is the total capital expenditure Akamai attributes to this commitment, as a multiple of its cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities at 30 June 2026?
company: Akamai Technologies, Inc. (AKAM, Nasdaq; fiscal year ends December 31)
failure_mode: Terms are web/press-release facts (US$11.6 billion over seven years, with a potential expansion of up to US$9 billion for about US$20 billion in total; warrant for 7.7 million shares, about 5%, at US$111.33; 2026 capex up about US$1.7 billion; total related capex about US$5.5 billion; no change to 2026 revenue guidance), while the denominators come from the Q2 2026 release (2026 revenue guidance US$4,445-4,530 million; cash and marketable securities US$4.616 billion). Traps: using the US$20bn potential total instead of the committed US$11.6bn; using the US$1.7bn 2026 capex step-up instead of the US$5.5bn total; dividing by the full 7-year value or by 2025 revenue; the guidance midpoint is US$4,487.5M.
expected_source: Akamai press release of 24 Sept 2026 (8-K Ex. 99.1) and Akamai Q2 2026 results release of 6 Aug 2026 (8-K Ex. 99.1).
grading: Key points (all required): (a) US$11.6 billion of contractual commitment over seven years (optional expansion up to a further US$9 billion, about US$20 billion in total); (b) average annual commitment = 11.6 / 7 = about US$1.657 billion = about 36.9% of the US$4,487.5 million midpoint of 2026 revenue guidance (accept 36%-38%); (c) total related capex of about US$5.5 billion = about 1.19x cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities of US$4.616 billion at 30 June 2026 (accept 1.15x-1.23x). Fail if US$20bn, the US$1.7bn capex step-up, or a different guidance range is used, or if the term is not seven years.
why_analysts_ask: The deal is a step-change in Akamai's AI-cloud strategy, and analysts size annual revenue run-rate and the funding burden relative to the balance sheet.
answer: (a) US$11.6 billion over seven years (plus a potential US$9 billion expansion, about US$20 billion in total) [W19-E1]. (b) 11.6 / 7 = about US$1.657 billion a year, about 36.9% of the US$4,487.5 million midpoint of Akamai's 2026 revenue guidance (US$4,445-4,530 million) [W19-E2]. (c) Total capex tied to the commitment is about US$5.5 billion, about 1.19x the US$4.616 billion of cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities at 30 June 2026 [W19-E1, W19-E2]. Akamai said it expects no impact on 2026 revenue guidance and about US$1.7 billion of extra 2026 capex.
